documents.prompt: Researchers record the average amount of sleep and the test score for each of {{n}} students but do not assign students to sleep for different amounts of time. The data show that students who sleep more tend to have higher test scores. Which conclusion is best supported?

choices.label: In this study, amount of sleep is associated with test score, but the study does not establish that more sleep causes higher scores.
More sleep causes higher test scores for all students.
Higher test scores cause students to sleep more.
The study proves that sleep and test score are unrelated.

solutionReview.headline: Recorded, not assigned: an association, not a cause.
reasoning: The researchers only recorded sleep and scores for {{n}} students; they did not assign amounts of sleep. That is an observational study.
An observational study can show an association, but other factors (study habits, for example) could explain it, so it cannot establish cause.
So: In this study, amount of sleep is associated with test score, but the study does not establish that more sleep causes higher scores.
solutionReview.commonError: Reading the association as cause and effect: only randomly assigning the treatment supports a causal claim.
solutionReview.answerSummary: In this study, amount of sleep is associated with test score, but the study does not establish that more sleep causes higher scores.

documents.prompt: Researchers randomly assign {{n}} volunteers to receive either treatment A or treatment B. The groups are otherwise treated the same, and the treatment A group has a higher average response. Which conclusion is best supported by the study design?

choices.label: The random assignment supports a cause-and-effect conclusion about the treatments for the study participants.
The result can automatically be generalized to every member of the population.
The study can show only an association because treatments were assigned at random.
No comparison between treatments is possible because volunteers participated.

solutionReview.headline: Random assignment supports cause and effect for the participants.
reasoning: The {{n}} volunteers were randomly assigned to treatment A or B and otherwise treated the same.

Random assignment balances other factors between the groups, so the difference can be attributed to the treatment for these participants. Volunteers are not a random sample, so it does not automatically generalize.
So: The random assignment supports a cause-and-effect conclusion about the treatments for the study participants.
solutionReview.commonError: Thinking random assignment shows only an association, or that the result automatically applies to a whole population.
solutionReview.answerSummary: The random assignment supports a cause-and-effect conclusion about the treatments for the study participants.

documents.prompt: A researcher selects a random sample of {{n}} residents from a city's adult population and asks whether they support a proposal. Which use of the sample is most justified?

choices.label: The sample results can be used to estimate the proportion of adults in the city who support the proposal.
The survey can establish that the proposal causes residents to change their opinions.
The results apply only to the sampled residents and cannot inform the city population.
The results can be generalized to every adult in the country.

solutionReview.headline: A random sample can estimate the city population's support.
reasoning: A random sample of {{n}} residents represents the city's adult population.
Its proportion of support estimates the city's proportion, with some sampling error. A survey cannot show cause, and the city is not the whole country.
So: The sample results can be used to estimate the proportion of adults in the city who support the proposal.
solutionReview.commonError: Generalizing beyond the population that was sampled, or claiming a survey shows cause and effect.
solutionReview.answerSummary: The sample results can be used to estimate the proportion of adults in the city who support the proposal.

documents.prompt: To estimate how all students at a school feel about lunch choices, a survey is given only to the {{n}} students who enter the cafeteria during the first 10 minutes of lunch. What is the main limitation of this sampling method?

choices.label: The sample may not be representative of all students at the school because it is a convenience sample.
The sample is automatically representative because every surveyed student attends the school.
The sample can establish which lunch option causes greater satisfaction.
The only limitation is that the sample contains more than one student.

solutionReview.headline: Whoever is easiest to reach is a convenience sample, which may not be representative.
reasoning: Only the {{n}} students who arrive in the first 10 minutes are surveyed: the ones easiest to reach.
Early arrivals may differ from other students (schedules, habits), so the sample may not represent the school.
So: The sample may not be representative of all students at the school because it is a convenience sample.
solutionReview.commonError: Assuming students from the school make a representative sample: how they are chosen matters.
solutionReview.answerSummary: The sample may not be representative of all students at the school because it is a convenience sample.

documents.prompt: In an experiment with {{n}} participants, the researchers randomly assign participants to a treatment group or a control group. What is the main purpose of the random assignment?

choices.label: To reduce systematic differences between the groups so treatment effects can be compared more fairly.
To make the participants a random sample of the entire population.
To guarantee that both groups will have exactly the same outcomes.
To increase the population size represented by the experiment.

solutionReview.headline: Random assignment makes the groups comparable.
reasoning: Random assignment decides by chance which of the {{n}} participants receive the treatment.
Chance tends to balance other characteristics between the groups, so a difference in outcomes can be traced to the treatment. It does not make the participants a random sample of a population.
So: To reduce systematic differences between the groups so treatment effects can be compared more fairly.
solutionReview.commonError: Confusing random assignment with random sampling: assignment supports fair comparisons; sampling supports generalization.
solutionReview.answerSummary: To reduce systematic differences between the groups so treatment effects can be compared more fairly.

documents.prompt: Researchers randomly sample {{n}} eligible adults from a population and then randomly assign the sampled adults to treatment or control groups. A meaningful difference in outcomes is observed. Which conclusion is best supported by this design?

choices.label: The random assignment supports a causal conclusion, and the random sampling supports generalizing the result to the population represented by the sample.
The design supports generalization but not a causal conclusion.
The design supports a causal conclusion but never permits population generalization.
The design supports neither causation nor generalization because both steps were random.

solutionReview.headline: Random sampling supports generalizing; random assignment supports cause.
reasoning: Randomly sampling {{n}} adults from the population supports generalizing to that population.
Randomly assigning them to treatment or control supports a cause-and-effect conclusion.
So: The random assignment supports a causal conclusion, and the random sampling supports generalizing the result to the population represented by the sample.
solutionReview.commonError: Mixing up the two roles: sampling is for generalizing, assignment is for causation.
solutionReview.answerSummary: The random assignment supports a causal conclusion, and the random sampling supports generalizing the result to the population represented by the sample.

documents.prompt: {{n}} volunteers respond to an advertisement for a study. The volunteers are then randomly assigned to treatment and control groups. Which statement best describes what the study design supports?

choices.label: Random assignment supports a causal comparison for the participants, but the volunteer sample limits how broadly the result can be generalized.
The volunteer sample makes the study a random sample of the population.
The study can be generalized broadly but cannot support a causal conclusion.
Random assignment removes the need for a comparison group.

solutionReview.headline: Random assignment without random sampling: causal for these volunteers only.
reasoning: The {{n}} participants volunteered after an advertisement, so they are not a random sample of any population.
They were randomly assigned to treatment and control, which supports a causal comparison among them.
So: Random assignment supports a causal comparison for the participants, but the volunteer sample limits how broadly the result can be generalized.
solutionReview.commonError: Treating volunteers as a random sample, or thinking random assignment rules out a causal conclusion.
solutionReview.answerSummary: Random assignment supports a causal comparison for the participants, but the volunteer sample limits how broadly the result can be generalized.

documents.prompt: A random sample of {{n}} adults is selected from a population. Researchers record each person's weekly exercise time and resting heart rate without assigning an exercise amount. The variables are associated in the sample. Which conclusion is best supported?

choices.label: The association can be used to describe the population represented by the random sample, but the observational design does not establish that exercise causes the difference in heart rate.
The random sample proves that additional exercise causes a lower resting heart rate.
Because the study is observational, the sample cannot provide any information about the population.
Random sampling and random assignment are the same feature of a study design.

solutionReview.headline: Random sample, observational design: describe the population, but no cause.
reasoning: The {{n}} adults are a random sample, so the association found can describe the population they represent.
Exercise was not assigned, so the study is observational and cannot show that exercise causes the difference.
So: The association can be used to describe the population represented by the random sample, but the observational design does not establish that exercise causes the difference in heart rate.
solutionReview.commonError: Treating random sampling as if it were random assignment: sampling supports generalizing, not causation.
solutionReview.answerSummary: The association can be used to describe the population represented by the random sample, but the observational design does not establish that exercise causes the difference in heart rate.
